The location and a growth of a settlement depends upon on its site and situation. The site is
actual land where people decide to build settlement. The situation can be defined as the
location of a place in relation to its surroundings. The situation of a settlement is the most
important for its future and growth. Situation involves many factors such as physical features
(mountains, rivers, sea coast) economic activity (agriculture, mining, industry), transportation
routes, (roads, railways, sea port). Location is often mentioned with reference to longitude and
latitude. In daily use, it is measured as a distance and direction from a known point.
3.1 Suitable Conditions for a Settlement
Geographers often study the factors that lead settlement towards becoming a large city over
time or remaining as a small village. Favourable factors that influence the location of a
settlementinclude:
1.FoodandWater Supply
Water is the basic need of life.
Settlements are therefore located near a
source of water like rivers. Rivers provide
constant supplyof water for drinking and
agricultural purposes. That is why we find
large number of settlements in river
valleys. Many of the main cities and
towns of the world are built around
rivers. For example Lahore was built on
river Raviand London on RiverThames.
